basis: User goals, defined before reading archived scenario contents; one Codex writer, no multiagent blind-testing claim

canaries.expected: Create form Cancel has no RPC; generated link is email-bound; new invitee joins only intended room. Known gateway dependency stays BLOCKED.

canaries.goal: Message save, refresh and re-login with failure recovery
canaries.expected: One durable message after double click/timeout/offline retry; Back/Cancel does not discard silently; refreshed/re-authenticated reader sees exact content.

canaries.goal: Inquiry submission and buyer task readback
canaries.expected: Supplier submits a unique request, buyer sees persisted task; refresh/re-login agree; repeated key never duplicates.
Supplier cannot inspect buyer internal room, another submitter inquiry or unauthorized room export; no unauthorized write.
Downloaded archive reflects actual room data, bytes and hashes; partial/missing attachment never claims complete. Actual gateway remains BLOCKED.
Expired/missing/cancelled recovery does not change current account; valid synthetic recovery changes only named account; no external mail.

canaries.goal: Sign in, sign out and re-login
canaries.expected: Synthetic signed OIDC to actual Postgres application; same account readback, separate account empty state; real provider/email remains BLOCKED.

canaries.goal: Discover, cancel, fork and half-day modification
canaries.expected: Public example retains sources/pending status; Cancel has no committed fork; applied half-day route and timezone persist; unknown weather does not invent places.

canaries.goal: Save, refresh and second-session trip restoration
canaries.expected: Chosen itinerary survives refresh/logout/re-login and prior-trip restoration; exact nodes and library read from actual isolated backend.
Second user cannot read/update or restore first user data; export contains exact itinerary/source metadata without cross-account content.

canaries.goal: Double-click, timeout, offline and conflict recovery
canaries.expected: Unknown-result save retries original key once; pending changes survive refresh; competing state cannot be silently overwritten.
Fresh synthetic OIDC recovery invalidates old sessions and pending login; unrelated account survives; provider-password/email service explicitly separate.
